venue.name: Arrowsmith Potters' Guild
venue.description: The Arrowsmith Potters' Guild is a member run pottery studio and shop in the old VIA Rail train station in Parksville, founded in 1995. The studio has eight wheels, three kilns, a slab roller and a large potting table, and the Train Station Pottery Shop sells members' work seven days a week. Courses and workshops run through the year, but the guild states that classes are for adults only with a minimum age of 19 unless a class says otherwise. On that basis this is not a venue for a school or daycare group.

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Our gift shop is currently accessible by walkers, but not wheelchairs.

restrictions: At this time, classes are for adults only (min. 19 years old) unless stated otherwise.
Please do not attend classes or use the studio if you are unwell.
venue.hours_notes: The Train Station Pottery Shop is open Monday to Saturday 10 am to 4 pm, and Sunday noon to 4 pm. The studio is open during shop hours; outside those hours a member with a key has to be present.

images.alt: Two hands shaping a cylinder of grey clay on a potter's wheel, with a white plastic tub of water beside the wheel head.

gaps: Classes here are adults only, minimum 19 years old, so there is nothing a children's group can book. That sentence sits at the foot of the classes page and applies to every course and workshop listed.

The shop itself is open to visitors of any age, but nothing on the site describes a demonstration, a tour or a visit that a group could arrange, and there is no children's or family offering anywhere on the site.
The only email route is a contact form. No address is published, so there is nobody to write to directly to ask whether they would ever make an exception for older students.
Washrooms, somewhere to eat and parking are not mentioned anywhere on the site. The only accessibility note says the gift shop takes walkers but not wheelchairs.
A plain fetch of the classes page returned exactly the same course list as the live page rendered in a browser, so there was no stale copy to work around.
The Open Graph image is a line drawing of the train station with the guild wordmark, so it was skipped as a hero. The hero is the studio photograph from the classes page instead.
Two other studio photographs on the classes page are only about 300 pixels across, too small to use.
The photograph used has no real alt text on the site, only the word Picture, so the alt was written after looking at the image.
The map on the contact page carries a marker with the guild's own coordinates, which is where the point comes from.
